crux: depth of the cat on the teacher's desk relative to the chair: desk rear flush with the wall (C2) vs desk placed from its leg floor contact (C1, round 1)
fault_found: C2's flush desk puts any desk leg's floor contact at y<=1013, but the desk front leg is visibly crisp down to y 1026-1027 (occluded there), so the desk stands in front of the wall (rear at 0.944-0.967 Zw); the flush model gives 0.457 with the same edges
lesson: When a decisive floor contact is hidden by an occluder, the occluder edge is only a one-sided bound; bound it from the other side with a second part of the same rigid object (such as a paired leg whose image ratio is known) that is also hidden or visible, and do not mistake the occluder edge for the contact.
